## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The new `--exclude` flag needs an environment-variable default, because the project's cli-flags rule requires one for every new flag under `cli/` and CI can't set the option without it. No other defects were found in the exclusion logic or its tests.

## Changes
The pull request adds a repeatable `--exclude GLOB` flag that makes `collect` skip any file whose basename matches a pattern. It also documents the flag in `docs/flags.md`, adds tests for the parser, `collect` and `main`, and adds a text fixture under `tests/fixtures/`.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- cli/main.py:17 — correctness — Default `--exclude` from `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` — If CI sets `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE=*.log`, the flag ignores it because the argument uses `default=[]` and never reads the environment. This breaks `.claude/skills/cli-flags/SKILL.md:11`: "Every command-line flag added under `cli/` from now on must also take its default from an `ARCHIVE_<NAME>` environment variable". — CI pipelines that set options through the environment can't exclude files, so excluded files still end up in their archives. — Fix: Build the default list by splitting `os.environ.get("ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE", "")` on a documented separator, and keep in mind that `action="append"` adds CLI patterns to that default rather than replacing it; then document the variable in `docs/flags.md:7` and extend `test_exclude_defaults_to_nothing`.
